newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to halt four-week T-bill issues June 30.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to halt four-week T-bill issues June 30.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry will halt four-week discount T-bill issues from June 30, prior to introduction of a currency board system, to ease domestic debt servicing, a central bank official said on Friday.
"The step is aimed at easing debt payments. The longer the maturity, the easier debt servicing," Nikolina Micheva, head of BNB's State Credits department, told Reuters.
The last five four-week maturities, to be offered by the Finance Ministry at next week's daily auctions will have a par value of 10 billion levs each, down from 15 billion levs this week.

But the par value of the three- and six-month discount T-bills offers for the regular Monday's auctions was raised to a total of 45 billion levs from 16 billion levs this week to compensate the lower par of four-week paper.
The Finance Ministry has issued four-week discount T-bills daily since January 20. One-week discount T-bill issues, which were also launched on January 20, were halted from May 26.
The 1997 budget draft envisages interest payments on domestic debt for this year at 6.9 percent of the projected gross domestic product of 16.150 trillion levs, or around 1.114 trillion levs.
Domestic government debt stood at 2,984 billion levs on June 9.

A Finance Ministry official has said that the net bank financing of the budget deficit during this year will be negative, meaning that funds collected through debt instruments will be less than dues paid to financial institutions.

A minus 0.5 percent of net bank financing of the budget deficit was set in the 1997 budget draft as part of implementation of an IMF-prescribed currency board system which bans central bank lending to the government and banks.
Under the currency board system, to be launched on July 1, liquidity in the banking system will be regulated through the market of government securities and interbank deposits.
